raw_case_text:
The participant we describe here was a healthy 24-year-old woman (height 174 cm, weight 56 kg) with no history of drug allergy and alcohol use. Laboratory tests conducted during screening on July 17, 2009, found that she was negative for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B. Her hepatic enzymes and creatinine clearance were within normal limits.
After about 8 weeks of taking TDF-FTC, this participant complained of mild paresthesiae, numbness, and a tingling sensation in her upper limbs that was associated with pain and cold. The symptoms did not affect her daily activities, physical examination was normal, and she had not taken any medications that are known to cause peripheral neuropathy upon interaction with TDF-FTC. After an additional 4 days, she developed a disabling weakness of her upper limbs and bilateral weakness of power grip of grade 3-4 and fine tremors in her hands at rest and with activity. Neurological examinations found normal orientation in time and place as was her pupillary light reaction and fundoscopy. Muscle tone, reflexes, and somatic sensations were also normal, but there was a mild deviation of the mouth and the tongue to the left, on protrusion.
After trial closure, analysis of her plasma and intracellular drug levels at week 4 and 8 were consistent with moderate adherence to TDF-FTC. At week 10, TDF-FTC was temporarily withheld due to safety concerns and as per the study protocol. The participant was given oral Neurorubine  (Vitamins B1, B6, and B12; Mepha Ltd, Aesch, Switzerland) for 2 weeks. Within 2 weeks after stopping the study drug, she was free of all symptoms. At week 12, she was restarted on the study drug according to the protocol. However, 1 month after restarting the pill, the participant complained of other neurological symptoms of posture-dependent numbness of her upper limbs. The numbness occurred while bending down and resolved after assuming an upright posture. She did not experience the earlier disabling muscle weakness or tremors. Her neurological exam was normal, and she continued taking the study drug. Her drug levels at week 24 (analyzed on stored samples after study closure) were consistent with low adherence to TDF-FTC.
At week 25, the study team decided to withdraw the study drug until neurologic exploration was completed. At week 28, the participant reported having taken a traditional herbal medicine, orally as a single dose. The nature of the herbal medication could not be determined by the study team.
At week 29, the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of her brain and cervical spine was found to be normal. Blood tests (performed at that time) revealed her lactate dehydrogenase was elevated at 514 U/L (normal range: 230-460), but her aldolase and creatinine phosphokinase were normal. The neurologist - with extensive experience in the treatment of HIV-infected patients - who assessed the participant observed:
The clinical manifestation in this patient was not the usual peripheral neuropathy known in patients receiving TDF-FTC. A typical TDF-FTC-related neuropathy starts with feet and only later goes to upper extremities. The fact that the paresthesiae occurs when the patient bends forward (Lhermitte's sign) suggests a possible lesion of the cervical spine, though MRI findings were normal.
In addition to the study drug, Neurorubine , and the unknown herbal medication, the participant reported taking the following medications: 1) medroxyprogesterone acetate, from enrolment throughout the study period; 2) ibuprofen at week five for one day; 3) amoxicillin/clavulanic acid at week seven for 10 days; and 4) diclofenac at weeks 9 and 10 for 3 and 7 days respectively.
Overall, for safety concern, the participant was managed as if she was assigned the TDF-FTC arm. The clinical team decided not to un-blind the participant's study group allocation, because this would not influence clinical case management. The participant's postural numbness gradually improved and was completely resolved by her week 36 visit. The participant finished study follow-up on September 28, 2010. Her symptoms did not reoccur after she discontinued the study pill.
After trial closure, levels of vitamin B12 on her stored blood samples at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16 all showed normal values: 625, 727, 744, and 791 ng/L respectively (normal range: 239-931 ng/L).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 24-year-old healthy HIV-negative woman enrolled in an HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) clinical trial developed upper extremity paresthesias, numbness, pain, grip weakness, and hand tremors 8 weeks after initiating tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine (TDF-FTC), followed by posture-dependent upper limb numbness (Lhermitte's sign) upon rechallenge.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Eight weeks after starting daily oral TDF-FTC in a blinded PrEP trial, the participant developed mild paresthesias, numbness, tingling, pain, and cold sensation in both upper extremities, progressing 4 days later to disabling bilateral upper limb weakness, weak handgrip, and resting/action hand tremors. TDF-FTC was held at week 10 and oral vitamin B1/B6/B12 (Neurorubine) was given for 2 weeks with complete symptom resolution. Four weeks after restarting study drug at week 12, she developed posture-dependent upper limb numbness triggered by neck/trunk flexion (Lhermitte's sign) without weakness or tremor, prompting permanent withdrawal of the study drug at week 25.
subjective.past_medical_history: Healthy 24-year-old female; negative baseline screening (July 17, 2009) for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B; no history of alcohol use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for bilateral upper extremity paresthesias, pain, transient grip weakness, fine hand tremors, and subsequent flexion-induced Lhermitte's sign. Concomitant medications during study: depot medroxyprogesterone acetate, short courses of ibuprofen (week 5), amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (week 7), diclofenac (weeks 9–10), Neurorubine (weeks 10–12), and a single dose of an unspecified oral herbal remedy at week 28. No drug allergies.

objective.physical_examination: Height 174 cm, weight 56 kg. Initial exam at week 8 was normal; exam 4 days later revealed bilateral upper extremity and power grip weakness (MRC grade 3–4/5), fine resting and action hand tremors, and mild leftward deviation of the mouth and protruding tongue, with intact orientation, pupillary reflexes, fundoscopy, muscle tone, deep tendon reflexes, and pinprick/light-touch sensation. Neurological exam during the week 16–25 postural numbness phase was normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline hepatic transaminases, creatinine clearance, HIV, syphilis, and HBV tests were normal/negative. Stored serum vitamin B12 levels at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16 were normal (625, 727, 744, and 791 ng/L; reference 239–931 ng/L). Week 29 blood tests showed mildly elevated LDH at 514 U/L (reference 230–460 U/L) with normal serum aldolase and creatine phosphokinase (CPK). Retrospective plasma and intracellular drug assays confirmed moderate TDF-FTC adherence at weeks 4 and 8 and low adherence at week 24.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain and cervical spine MRI performed at week 29 was completely normal without demyelinating or compressive cord lesions.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Atypical reversible upper-extremity sensorimotor neuropathy and Lhermitte-like postural paresthesias temporally associated with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine (TDF-FTC) pre-exposure prophylaxis in an HIV-negative 24-year-old woman (confirmed by positive dechallenge at week 10 and week 25, positive rechallenge at week 16, normal vitamin B12 levels, and normal brain/cervical spine MRI). Following permanent discontinuation of TDF-FTC at week 25, her postural upper limb numbness gradually resolved completely by week 36 with no recurrence through study completion on September 28, 2010.
